draft.title: Choosing a separation method
card: To separate a mixture, look for a property that is different in each part. The method is chosen to use that difference.
Particle size
if one part is solid and too big to pass through paper or a sieve, use filtration or sieving. Water treatment plants use screens and filters to remove solid bits.
Density

if the parts differ in how heavy they are for their size, a heavy solid can settle so the liquid can be decanted. Yandying is a method used by First Nations Australians. Seeds are shaken and tossed in a shallow wooden dish called a coolamon, so the light husks separate from the heavier seeds.
Solubility and boiling point
if a solid is dissolved, evaporation can recover it. If a liquid must be collected from a solution, distillation uses its lower boiling point.
draft.remember: Find the property that differs, then pick the method that uses it.

a.q: Sand is mixed with small pebbles. The pebbles are too big to fit through the holes of a sieve, but the sand fits. Which property is used to separate them?
opts: Particle size
Boiling point
Solubility in water
Density in a liquid
a.why: The sieve holds back the larger pebbles and lets the smaller sand pass, so the difference in particle size is used. Boiling point and solubility are not involved because nothing is heated or dissolved.
a.clue: What does the sieve do to big pieces compared with small ones?

b.q: Priya has a jar of salty water. She wants to collect the pure water, not just the salt. Which method suits this best?
opts: Distillation, as water boils at a lower temperature than salt
Filtration, as the salt is too large to pass through paper
Evaporation, as the water escapes and is collected as vapour
Decanting, as the salt settles below the water
b.why: Distillation boils the water and condenses the vapour into a container, so the water is collected. Plain evaporation lets the water escape into the air, so it would not be collected. Filtration does not work because the salt is dissolved, so it passes through the paper with the water.
b.clue: Which method collects the liquid rather than losing it to the air?

proposal.title: Choosing a separation method
card: To separate a mixture, look for a property that is different in each part. Then choose the method that uses that difference.
Particle size
if a solid is too big to pass through paper or a sieve, use filtration or sieving. Dissolved particles are too small to be caught, so they pass through.
Density

a heavier solid can settle so the liquid is poured off, called decanting. In yandying, First Nations Australians shake seeds in a wooden dish called a coolamon, so light husks separate from heavier seeds.
Solubility and boiling point
evaporation recovers a dissolved solid, but the water escapes into the air. Distillation boils off the liquid with the lower boiling point and cools the vapour to collect it.
proposal.remember: Find the property that differs, then pick the method that uses it.

a.q: Sand is mixed with small pebbles. The pebbles are too big to fit through the holes of a sieve, but the sand fits. Which property is used to separate them?
opts: Particle size
Boiling point
Solubility in water
Density in a liquid
a.why: The sieve holds back the larger pebbles and lets the smaller sand pass, so the difference in particle size is used. Boiling point and solubility are not involved because nothing is heated or dissolved.
a.clue: What does the sieve do to big pieces compared with small ones?

b.q: Priya has a jar of salty water. She wants to collect the pure water, not just the salt. Which method suits this best?
opts: Distillation, as water boils at a lower temperature
Filtration, as salt is too large to pass through paper
Evaporation, as the water vapour is caught and kept
Decanting, as the salt sinks to the bottom of the jar
b.why: Distillation boils the water and cools the vapour so it can be collected. Plain evaporation keeps the salt but lets the water escape into the air. Filtration and decanting fail because dissolved salt neither gets caught by paper nor settles.
b.clue: Which method collects the liquid rather than losing it to the air?
